title: Restriction triangle inside a closed support
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, let $B,C\subseteq T$ be
closed subschemes, and
put $V=T\setminus C$, with open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow T$.
Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of module sheaves on the
small etale site.
Write $R\Gamma_B(T,F)$ for the derived functor of the
sections supported on $B$,
whose cohomology is the
cohomology with support.
There is a natural distinguished triangle in the
derived category of modules:

$$
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_B(T,F)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\cap V}(V,v^*F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(T,F)[1].
$$

The third support is closed in $V$; its ambient scheme is $V$.

proof.text: Construct closed intersection and open support by scheme pullbacks and compute their complements by the topological pullback image formula. Supported sections are actual kernels. The kernel universal property constructs inclusion and transport, uniquely characterized on global sections. Terminal-object uniqueness and the inverse-image unit identify transport with restriction on sections.

proof.text: Injective restriction to an open is surjective by the proved source theorem Sheaf.isSplitEpi_ΓRes_of_injective. Hom into the open etale object is a subsingleton, since its structure map is monic. The source theorem extends the section map along the sheafification of sigmaYonedaToConst. This implements the lifting step directly, without open-closed recollement.

Let U be T minus C, W be T minus B, and O=U union W. The square of the two opens and their intersection is a pullback and covers O. The sheaf amalgamation axiom gives a pullback square of sections. Convert an inverse-image supported section on U to an ordinary section using the etale localization-restriction comparison. Its restriction to U intersection W vanishes. Glue it to zero on W, then lift the resulting section on O to T by step 2. The lift vanishes on W, hence lies in the B-support kernel, and restricts to the given section.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: explicit extension of supported sections, using the open cover V union (T minus B)

proof.text: The composite of intersection support inclusion and open restriction is zero by their kernel characterizations. Conversely a B-supported section whose restriction to U vanishes is zero on U and W, hence on O by sheaf uniqueness. This identifies the kernel with intersection support, while its inclusion is monic. Together with step 3 this gives a short exact sequence on injectives. Apply it degreewise to obtain the short exact complex.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: kernel of restriction and resulting short exact sequence of section complexes

proof.text: Etale extension by zero is an exact left adjoint to open inverse image, which therefore preserves K-injective complexes. The source rightDerivedFunctorCompIso and exact-functor comparison give the open-composite derived comparison. The right-derived universal property proves its unique unit normalization. For a scheme isomorphism the global-section and complementary-section maps are isomorphisms, so their kernel map and its derived map are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), part (2), and 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), part (1), for bounded-below injective computation; Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor) for the triangle

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-unbounded-derived-boundary] to the support short complex, short exact on injectives by step 4. This gives the unique natural boundary normalized on every termwise injective K-injective complex. For a bounded-below object choose its injective model. Derived computation identifies the first two arrows and the boundary normalization identifies the third with the canonical short exact complex triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Transport distinguishedness along the model isomorphism and the open-composite comparison.
